title: interaction-atelier-mini-prd
body:
TL;DR:
Rough sketch for an "Interaction Atelier" — a small feature set that lets product teams define and test multiple lightweight response modes (micro-fidelity presets, tone variants, cost caps) and route traffic between them to quickly evaluate UX and unit economics. This is a personal brainstorm / proto-PRD for an MVP experiment.

Problem we keep hitting:
- Product teams want to A/B cheap vs. rich responses without shipping hard server-side changes or model rollouts.
- Current mechanism (separate model endpoints + infra work) is slow and expensive for quick experiments.
- Need fast iteration: author variant, attach to route, measure UX + cost, rollback easily.

Goals (MVP):
1) Provide a small UI and API to define "presets" (name + constraints) that map to runtime hints: max_tokens, temperature, model_variant_fallback, quantization_hint, opportunistic-caching.
2) Enable on-request variant selection by rule (random weighted, user param, header flag).
3) Capture per-variant telemetry: token usage, latency P95/P50, error rate, sticky retention (did users re-request or abandon).
4) Fast rollback + kill switch; variant-level cost caps (soft limit) and fallback chain.

Non-goals for MVP:
- Full rollout UI across orgs (opt for single-team scope).
- Automated quality detection (leave to evals/QA).

Personas:
- Growth PM: wants to test cheaper response to 10% of users for pricing experiments.
- Product engineer: wants low-friction way to wire variant into existing route with minimal SDK changes.
- Platform engineer: needs safety controls and observability hooks.

User stories (rough):
- As a PM, I can create a "Compact" preset that caps tokens to 60 and routes to a cheaper model when available so I can measure retention impact.
- As an engineer, I can attach 0.2 weight to the Compact preset on /chat endpoint with a single config change.
- As SRE, I can set a daily budget for the Compact preset and an automatic toggle-off if cost exceeds X.
- As product analyst, I can slice usage by preset in Console and export variant-level metrics.

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- Preset creation via Console form and via API with at least: id, display_name, max_tokens, model_hint, weight_fallback_order.
- Console shows per-preset token/day and P95 latency.
- SDK/REST header to force a preset for dev/testing.
- Preset can be disabled immediately via Console (kill switch).

Instrumentation + metrics to capture:
- tokens_generated_per_request, request_latency_ms, model_switch_count, preset_ejection_count (when fallback used), cost_estimate_per_request, retention_1d/7d by preset cohort.

MVP technical approach (sketch):
- Config layer: simple JSON schema persisted in config store (existing route config + presets array).
- Runtime: quick rule-eval step in router that selects preset per request, attaches runtime hints to inference request. No new model binaries.
- Observability: emit variant tag on traces and telemetry pipeline; Console visualization will read aggregated data.
- Safety: quota check before eval; if preset budget near exhausted, reduce weight to 0 or route to fallback.

Edge cases / open questions:
- How to represent quality constraints? (e.g., "minimum perplexity" is impossible) — likely keep quality as manual eval label until we integrate micro-evals.
- Can some variants require different function-calling behavior? should we allow that? probably not in MVP.
- Interaction with Dedicated/Private customers: presets should be metadata-only; no cross-tenant impurity. Need access controls.
- SDK changes: ideally add a small header X-Redwood-Preset to force assignment. Does this conflict with existing auth proxies? check infra.

Mini rollout plan:
- Week 0: spec + proto config schema + sample Console form (static).
- Week 1: router rule-eval and header passthrough; basic telemetry tags. Smoke on staging.
- Week 2: Console form & listing, preset create API, basic metrics aggregation. Internal dogfood.
- Week 3: open to 2 product teams for experiments; iterate based on feedback.

Risks / mitigations:
- Risk: variants could increase overall latency if they trigger extra fallback hops. Mitigate: add opt-in flag for synchronous-only presets and add a P95 SL threshold that auto-disable.
- Risk: cost misestimation. Mitigate: conservative cost-guess on day 0 + soft caps.

Notes to self / TODOs:
- Check with infra if lightweight per-request config eval at router adds CPU pressure. Talk to Tomasz/Kelsey.
- Mock Console screens (Asha) — attach prototype.
- Add elbow room for Private customers in permission model.
- Draft experiment template for PMs: hypothesis, cohort size, success metric, kill criteria.

Quick links / references:
- Related idea: "budgeted-response-tiering" (see convo in #economy-mode) — overlap on cost caps.
- GH PR that added X-Redwood-Route headers: GH:repo/redwood/PR-2843
- Simpler feature we can ship first: forceable presets via header + telemetry labeling (no Console).

If this feels useful I'll tidy into a two-pager and sketch Console mocks. For now: rough notes to iterate in sprint planning.

-- Milo
